title: The Riverside Orange Groves
story:
Stepping off the cool ancient stones of El Puente Viejo, James felt the sharp shift in air. The dusty valley trail broadened, giving way to high rows of glossy dark-green orange trees that stretched alongside the rushing river. The warm afternoon air smelled thick and sweet, heavy with citrus and damp earth. Nico scampered ahead along low concrete irrigation ditches, his whiskers twitching at every shadow, bursting with restless energy now that they had left the gloomy streets of El Pedregal far behind.

James paused beneath a low-hanging branch, his hand instinctively reaching to feel the smooth brass canister tucked against his side. Barnaby's map was growing longer with every step south, yet looking down through the leafy canopy at the sun-dappled river, he knew they had entered a kinder stretch of land. Beneath a cluster of heavy orange trees, sweet fruit lay scattered in the clover. James knelt and selected a small, ripe orange that had fallen intact from the branch, peeling the bright skin back with his nimble fingers while Nico watched intently from atop a smooth stone.

They shared the juicy fruit in the warm shade, the sharp sweetness bursting against the dry dust of the trail. James remembered the sweet wild berries from the Oakhaven market vendors, but eating fresh fruit in the sun with a small companion felt different—a little quieter, and remarkably earned. Nico chattered cheerfully, darting back and forth across the stone rim of a narrow irrigation canal that wound its way through the grove toward a whitewashed brick shed nearby.

As the sun began to dip toward the western hills, painting the river water in shades of bronze and rose, James led the way to the irrigation shed. Its terracotta tiled roof was slightly weathered, but the overhang provided a dry, sheltered nook away from the night breezes. James carefully set his pack down, unwinding the sprig of wild highland sage to take in its calming scent, while Nico curled up inside a shallow hollow in an old wooden fruit crate. Resting against the cool brickwork of the shed, James looked out at the glowing river, content with the day's journey.
location: Tiled irrigation shed in the riverside orange groves past El Puente Viejo
